old_caption: The video showcases a close-up view of a colorful popsicle resting on a white plate. The popsicle features three distinct horizontal layers: a green layer at the top, followed by a red layer, and finally a yellow layer at the bottom. The popsicle stick is wooden and protrudes from the right side of the popsicle. As the video progresses, there is a noticeable change in the appearance of the popsicle. Initially, the layers remain intact, but as time passes, the ice begins to melt, causing a subtle, even softening across all layers without significant blending or spreading.
original_wisa_caption: The video showcases a close-up view of a colorful popsicle resting on a white plate. The popsicle features three distinct horizontal layers: a green layer at the top, followed by a red layer, and finally a yellow layer at the bottom. The popsicle stick is wooden and protrudes from the right side of the popsicle. As the video progresses, there is a noticeable change in the appearance of the popsicle. Initially, the layers remain intact, but as time passes, the ice begins to melt, causing the colors to blend slightly. The green layer starts to soften and spread downward, while the red and yellow layers also show signs of melting, though they remain mostly separate. The overall scene remains static, focusing solely on the popsicle and its gradual transformation due to the melting process.
caption: The video showcases a horizontal multi-segment popsicle resting on a plain white plate, its speckled olive-green rounded tip at the left and a flat wooden stick protruding to the right. From left to right the body reads as a red band, a bright yellow band, and a pale cream-yellow band. A thin glossy line of meltwater tracks along the bottom edge of the body, most pronounced beneath the yellow and cream segments. This sheen gradually widens, and a small clear puddle spreads on the plate under the pale-yellow portion. The meltwater line becomes more continuous and reflective along the lower edge. The popsicle itself remains broadly in the same position and orientation, with no obvious translation or rotation of the left tip or the stick end. The change across the footage appears mainly from melting rather than movement.

From left to right the body reads as a red band, a bright yellow band, and a pale cream-yellow band. A thin glossy line of meltwater tracks along the bottom edge of the body, most pronounced beneath the yellow and cream segments.
